caption: I would have bet money the eating out was R900. What's the number you'd rather not check?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R26 500
p/m salary
Living in Durban
slides.body:
Female, 31
Single, no kids
Job: Registered nurse
Net salary: R26 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: I could pay R4 500 in Phoenix, but I'd add two hours of driving to a job where I already do twelve hour shifts.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Night shift and public transport don't mix. This one isn't negotiable for me.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, and the Woolies top-ups I pretend don't count
slides.body: I shop once a month, then four more times because I forgot something.

slides.title: Eating out
slides.includes: Hospital canteen, delivery after night shift
slides.body: I would have told you R900. I checked. It was R2 400. Night shift makes you buy things.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My mom's electricity, my nephew's school transport
slides.body: It goes off the day after payday so I never have to treat it as a choice. I'd rather it that way.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & insurance, medical aid, electricity, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, gym, savings
slides.body: Eight line items I never think about one at a time. Together they're almost a third of what I earn.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R26 500. That's about R55 a day until payday, and payday is never as close as I think it is.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The eating out number was the one that got me.

No bank login needed.
